findings.element: interaction-check.mjs:1231 and :1250 — the `august-inside-a-july-reading` and `refusals-written-in-the-studio-vocabulary` blocks; same text at panel/round-1-batch4-assertions.js:96 and :115
findings.problem: Both blocks build their patterns with four source backslashes: `new RegExp("\\\\b" + m + "\\\\b(?!\\\\s+\\\\d{4})", "g")` and `new RegExp("\\\\b" + w + "\\\\b", "i")`. Four backslashes in JS source yield the two-character escape `\\`, so the compiled pattern is a LITERAL backslash followed by `b`, not a word boundary. I cut lines 1231 and 1250 out of the file byte-for-byte with sed (od -c confirms four 0x5C bytes), ran them unmodified under node, and got: `re.source` = `\\bAugust\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})`; `.test("finished in August, before")` = false; the banned-vocabulary filter run over "the callers accrues periods provider structured recorder" = []. Page text never contains a backslash, so `found` and `hits` are permanently empty. That is eight assertions — `no month is named without its year` and `the refusals speak the reader's language`, each across full/partial/quiet/first-run — that cannot fail for any content whatsoever. I then re-ran the SAME two checks with single escapes against the live surface in chromium at 1440 in all four states: bareMonths [], banned hits [], the only year-bearing strings being "June 2027" and (first-run) "August 2026". So the surface's behaviour is correct and only the checks are dead. The mechanism is lessons.md L-12 creeping back in its mirror form — over-escaped rather than under-escaped — through the one tool built to stop it: panel/append-assertions.mjs's own header comment says a regex written through a shell "silently made the checks vacuous. lessons.md L-12", and the block it spliced carries the same defect.
findings.consequence: The engagement's record reads 461 assertions, all green. Eight of them are theatre. Two confirmed round-1 findings are carried as closed on the strength of checks that would sail through a total regression — put the month back without its year, or write the refusals in studio vocabulary again, and the gate still prints pass. Under L-05 ("a finding is closed only when something asserts it") those two are not closed, and the ledger this engagement ends on is overstating its own coverage by eight.
findings.fix: In interaction-check.mjs change line 1231 to `const re = new RegExp("\\b" + m + "\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})", "g");` and line 1250 to `const hits = banned.filter((w) => new RegExp("\\b" + w + "\\b", "i").test(text));` — two source backslashes each, not four. Make the identical edit at panel/round-1-batch4-assertions.js:96 and :115 so a re-splice cannot reintroduce it. Write both edits with a file-editing tool, never through a heredoc.
findings.assertion: Add a self-test immediately above the two blocks, so the gate proves its own patterns before it trusts them: `ok("the gate's own word-boundary patterns compile as word boundaries", new RegExp("\\b" + "August" + "\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})").test("finished in August, before") === true && new RegExp("\\bAugust\\b(?!\\s+\\d{4})").test("in August 2026") === false && new RegExp("\\b" + "callers" + "\\b", "i").test("the callers did not answer") === true);`. Then prove the two repaired blocks can fail: with `F.comparisonArrives` temporarily set to "10 August", `no month is named without its year · first-run` must FAIL, and must pass again at "10 August 2026"; with the word "provider" injected into a LIMITS body, `the refusals speak the reader's language · full` must FAIL.

findings.element: lately.html — `hide()` in the tooltip block (~L1168) and the `pointerleave` listener on every `[data-tip]`
findings.problem: `hide()` guards only the touch pin: `if (pinned && !force) return; tip.classList.remove("on"); showing = null;`. It does not guard focus. Driven in chromium at 1440, ?state=full&v=light: Tab to `.dot` nth(2) — the ring paints (`:focus-visible` true) and the tip names "Send the midweek rate to the June 2027 couple, 5 days open". Move the real pointer onto that same mark (tip still on, correct), then 400px away. `pointerleave` fires, `hide()` clears the tip and nulls `showing`. Measured immediately after: tip `on` = false, `document.activeElement` still the same dot, still matching `:focus-visible`. It does not come back — `onMove` returns on `!showing`, so a subsequent 40px scroll leaves it off (measured). Only Tab-away-and-Tab-back recovers it. The same happens if the pointer merely crosses a DIFFERENT mark and leaves: I focused dot nth(1), hovered dot nth(8) (the tip correctly retargeted to "41 days open / Confirm the marquee sides…", overwriting the focused mark's label), then moved away — tip off, dot nth(1) still ringed and now unnamed.
findings.consequence: This is exactly the state the round-2 note says the scroll path was written to prevent: "dropping a focused mark's label leaves a visibly focused mark with no name anywhere on the screen." The job title lives in no other pixel on this surface. A keyboard reader who also rests a hand on the mouse — the ordinary case, not an edge — is left staring at a ringed 12px disc with no way to learn which job it is except to leave it and come back.
findings.fix: Hand the tip back to the focused mark instead of clearing it. Replace `const hide = (force = false) => { if (pinned && !force) return; tip.classList.remove("on"); showing = null; };` with `const hide = (force = false) => { if (pinned && !force) return; const held = document.activeElement; if (!force && held && held.dataset && held.dataset.tip) { show(held); return; } tip.classList.remove("on"); showing = null; };`. `drop()` is untouched, so Escape and a touch-away still dismiss outright, and `blur` still calls `hide()` — by then `document.activeElement` is no longer a mark, so it clears as it does today.
findings.assertion: For each of light and dark at 1440, ?state=full: focus `.dot` nth(2) by keyboard, assert `#tip` has class `on` and `#tip.textContent` contains the focused dot's `aria-label` title. Then move the real pointer onto that dot's centre and then to 400px away; after 250ms assert `#tip` STILL has class `on` and still names the focused dot. Repeat with the pointer travelling over `.dot` nth(8) before leaving — the tip must return to naming nth(2), not stay on nth(8) and not go off. Then press Escape and assert it does go off, so the explicit dismissal is not broken.

findings.element: the three `.tab` anchors in `shell()` — `<a class="tab t-body" href="#">`, including the one carrying `aria-current="page"`
findings.problem: All three tabs are anchors to a bare `#`. Driven in chromium at 1440, ?state=full&v=light: with the document scrolled to y=684, focusing "Today's Signal" and pressing Enter moves the URL to `…&v=light#`, sets `scrollY` to 0 and takes `history.length` from 2 to 3, while `aria-current` stays on "Lately" and not one pixel of the surface changes. A mouse click on "Full Briefing" does the same; so does a click on "Lately", the tab that is already current (2→3 history entries, trailing `#` appended). Pressing Back afterwards strips the `#` and changes nothing visible — one Back press consumed per activation. Separately, measuring rest/hover/press from what paints: the two sibling tabs go ink-3 → ink on hover and then do not move on press; the current tab measures `rgb(17,17,17)` at rest, on hover and under a held pointer — it is the only focusable control on this surface with no hover state and no press state at all. This is the same bare-`#` href round 2 removed from the KPI cards ("the cards were link roles whose href appended a bare `#`"); the fix landed on one object and not on the other.
findings.consequence: A reader who presses the sibling tabs to find out why nothing happened gets no press feedback that the click even landed, and silently spends one Back press per attempt. Three tries and their Back button appears broken — they press it three times, watch the same page each time, and conclude the app is stuck. Nothing on screen tells them any of this happened.
findings.fix: Give the tabs the same guard the marks already carry. After the `[data-tip]` listener loop in lately.html add: `for (const el of root.querySelectorAll(".tab")) el.addEventListener("click", (e) => e.preventDefault());`. The link role, the focus ring, the hover colour and the `aria-current` underline are all unchanged; what stops is the fragment, the history entry and the jump to the top. When the two sibling routes are wired on the port packet, swap their `href="#"` for the real routes and drop them from the selector — the current tab keeps the guard, because a tab that is already current has nowhere to go.
findings.assertion: At 1440 in every state, for each of the three `.tab` elements: record `location.href`, `document.scrollingElement.scrollTop` and `history.length`; activate the tab once by mouse click and once by focus + Enter; after 200ms assert all three values are unchanged, that `location.href` carries no trailing `#`, and that `document.querySelector('.tab[aria-current=page]').textContent.trim()` is still "Lately".

findings.element: `.card.ages` — the nine `.dot` buttons and the tip they raise
findings.problem: A job's title exists in exactly one place on this screen: the tip raised by hover, focus or a tap. Nothing at rest says the marks are pressable. Screenshotting `.card.ages` on its own at 1440 ?state=full, the whole card is: the heading "How long open work has been sitting", an "OLDEST · 41 DAYS" stamp, a dashed fortnight rule with its label, nine 12px discs, a hairline axis and four ticks. No legend, no instruction, no rest-state name — the only affordance is `cursor: pointer`, which does not exist under a coarse pointer, and a 2px ring/fill difference that reads as a data encoding (inside vs past the fortnight), not as a control. The accessibility tree is better served than the screen: every `aria-label` carries "<title>, open N days", so a screen-reader user is handed all nine titles and a sighted phone reader is handed none. Driven at 390 with touch, a tap does raise and pin the tip correctly — the mechanism is there and works; the invitation is missing.
findings.consequence: Movement two exists to answer "what has quietly slipped". It tells a phone reader that three jobs are past a fortnight and the oldest is 41 days, and gives them no discoverable route to WHICH three — the one fact the movement was built to deliver. They are left with nine anonymous ages and an instruction to go looking in Tasks.
findings.fix:
Add one stamp in the existing label voice inside `.card.ages`, immediately after the `.strip` div and before the card's `.sr` paragraph: `

Each mark is one job — press one for its name

`. No new colour, no new weight, no new object, no change to the strip's geometry or to the reserved band.
findings.assertion: For every state that draws a `.strip` (full, partial, quiet, first-run), at 390 and 1440 and on both grounds: assert `.card.ages` contains an element whose visible text matches `/press one for its name/i`, that it is not inside any `[aria-hidden="true"]`, that its computed `font-family` starts "Geist Mono" at `font-size: 11px` and `font-weight: 400`, and that its rendered box lies inside the `.card.ages` box with a top margin of 12px. Also assert `document.querySelectorAll('.dot').length > 0` in the same state, so the line can never be present where there are no marks.

biggestWin: Repair the two double-escaped regexes at interaction-check.mjs:1231 and :1250 (and their source at panel/round-1-batch4-assertions.js:96 and :115). Eight of the gate's 461 assertions currently cannot fail for any content, and they are the eight guarding two confirmed round-1 findings — so the closing ledger overstates its own coverage in precisely the class the engagement already paid for once and built append-assertions.mjs to prevent (lessons.md L-12). Everything else on this surface is a few lines of polish; this is the one item that changes what the record means.
